subject: CAIQ: proposed priority rubric & evidence sprint for Northlake Capital
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@northlake.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: security@northlake.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ mapping — priority areas and timeline

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Northlake's InfoSec team reviewed your CAIQ draft and we want to lock down two things before we move to the legal redlines: (1) a priority/severity rubric that maps CAIQ controls to what we expect for production-facing inference (latency-sensitive inference multitenant controls vs. admin/operator controls), and (2) a concrete evidence sprint plan so we can schedule our audit window in June.

Specifically, can you:
- Share a short rubric (low/med/high) for the ~30 controls we flagged as high-impact in the attached workbook.
- Confirm owner names inside Redwood for each high/critical control so we know who to loop in for evidence pulls (logs, config exports, key rotation proof).
- Give us an estimate for how long a sample evidence handoff would take (S3/SharePoint link preferred) and any redaction guidance for tenant identifiers.

We'd like your input in time for a 1-hour workshop Thurs 5/7.

Best,
Susan
Susan Lee
Director, Security Operations
Northlake Capital

Attachment: northlake-caiq-questions.xlsx (workbook with flagged controls)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@northlake.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping — priority areas and timeline

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear ask and the workbook. I've attached a first-pass rubric labeled 'caiq-priority-rubric-v1.pdf' and populated owner columns in your spreadsheet (northlake-caiq-answers-v1.xlsx).

High-level notes:
- We propose a three-tier priority: Critical (blocker for tenant isolation / key custody), High (operator controls and runtime telemetry needed for incident reconstruction), Medium (procedural controls, policy artifacts).
- For Critical control evidence we estimate an initial handoff window of 48 hours from owner confirmation; High controls ~3 business days (log extracts and config snapshots), Medium controls ~1 week. These are conservative estimates assuming owners can pull artifacts directly from our evidence portal.
- Redaction guidance: redact tenant IDs and replace with synthetic GUIDs, provide mapping index in a separate CSV. We can accept redacted artifacts; maintain original name/version metadata.

Action items we kicked off internally:
- Kimberly will validate cryptographic key rotation proofs and HSM attestations.
- Priyom will stage runtime telemetry extracts and sampling guidance.
- Marissa will coordinate DocuSign for an evidence access SLA and set up a shared S3 bucket with limited-time credentials.

Attaching: caiq-priority-rubric-v1.pdf; northlake-caiq-answers-v1.xlsx (owner column added); evidence-upload-instructions.txt (S3 presign process).

Would 10:00 AM PT on Thu 5/7 for the workshop work for your team? If so we'll send calendar invite and pre-reads.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: caiq-priority-rubric-v1.pdf; northlake-caiq-answers-v1.xlsx; evidence-upload-instructions.txt

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: CAIQ mapping — priority areas and timeline

Looping in specifics per Aditya's plan. Quick clarifications before the workshop:
- For KMS/HSM evidence we can provide rotating key metadata (key id, rotate timestamps, policy snapshots) and signed attestation from our KMS vendor. We will not share private key material.
- I'll prepare a 1-page checklist of exactly which log lines and config snapshots satisfy each Critical control (example: Control A-6 requires API gateway logs + agent-level connection trace for the sampled window).
- On sampling: for runtime telemetry we recommend a 48-hour contiguous window rather than disjoint samples to make incident tracebacks simpler. Priyom, can you confirm whether KV cache metadata will be included in the telemetry extracts?

Kimberly
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms-attestation-sample.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@northlake.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: CAIQ mapping — priority areas and timeline

Thanks everyone — the workshop earlier was productive. A few follow-ups and concrete links:
- We finalized the priority rubric (v1) and uploaded artifacts to a temporary S3 bucket. Links and presigned URLs will be shared to security@northlake.com; see evidence-upload-instructions.txt for the access pattern and TTLs.
- KV cache metadata: we will provide summarized KV cache manifests (no user data) that show cache hits, eviction snapshots, and TTLs for the sampled window. That satisfies the runtime isolation tracing requirement without exposing tenant prompt content.
- Owner commitments: Kimberly (KMS/HSM), Priyom (runtime telemetry + KV manifests), Marissa (S3 access + DocuSign agreement).

Next steps for Northlake:
1) Confirm acceptance of the priority rubric and owners by EOD Mon 5/10.
2) Provide list of controls you still want as 'Critical' beyond the 30 we flagged.
3) Identify any legal constraints on cross-border logs — everything we're staging is US-region by default; we can accommodate EU residency but will need an extra 48-72 hours.

Thanks — I'll circulate the S3 presigned links to security@northlake.com once we get the DocuSign signed.

— Priyom
Sr. Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-upload-instructions.txt (contains S3 presign sample commands and TTL guidance)
